claim: In Eq. (19) of Oszmaniec and Kuś, “On detection of quasiclassical states” (arXiv:1111.1005; J. Phys. A 45 (2012) 244034), the phrase “increasingly ordered eigenvalues” is incompatible with the displayed antiunitary convex-roof formula and must be read as nonincreasingly ordered, \(\mu_1\ge\mu_2\ge\cdots\ge\mu_r\). If the printed descriptor is instead read literally as \(\mu_1\le\mu_2\le\cdots\le\mu_r\), then for every use of the formula with \(r\ge2\), positivity gives \(\mu_1-\sum_{j=2}^r\mu_j\le\mu_1-\mu_2\le0\), so the stated roof collapses to zero. The cited Uhlmann proposition gives the same formula with descending eigenvalues. In the paper’s two-qubit setting, the Bell-white-noise family \(\rho_p=p|\Phi^+\rangle\langle\Phi^+|+(1-p)I/4\), with \(|\Phi^+\rangle=(|00\rangle+|11\rangle)/\sqrt2\), has spin-flip singular values \(b=(1+3p)/4\) and \(a=(1-p)/4\) threefold; hence the corrected formula gives \(\max\{0,(3p-1)/2\}\), while the literal printed ordering gives zero. At \(p=1/2\), the discrepancy is \(1/4\) versus \(0\). The correction concerns only the ordering descriptor in Eq. (19), not the paper’s representation-theoretic theorems.

correctness.rationale: The source text says increasingly ordered immediately after a largest-minus-the-rest roof. Uhlmann Proposition 4.1, cited by the source, requires descending eigenvalues. For literal ascending order and r>=2, positivity gives mu_1-sum_{j>=2} mu_j <= mu_1-mu_2 <= 0. The Bell-white-noise witness gives the corrected value max(0,(3p-1)/2), including 1/4 at p=1/2, while the literal order gives zero.

evidence: Uhlmann gives the general descending-order roof theorem and is explicitly cited by Oszmaniec–Kuś.
The accepted claim does not attempt to supersede Uhlmann; it concerns the inconsistent ordering descriptor in its later application.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader theorem determines which ordering is mathematically correct, but it does not make the source wording harmless: literal increasing order makes the displayed detector vanish for r>=2. The accepted item is therefore a source-specific correction, not a new general roof theorem.

value.rationale: The correction prevents a substantive failure mode: literal increasing order makes the mixed-state criterion zero for every r>=2. The Bell-white-noise witness shows a standard state for which a direct implementation would return 0 instead of 1/4. Restoring the ordering is therefore necessary for the detector to have the function claimed for it.
